This COMPLETES the dds-41245 bundle (Jul 4 - Sep 26 1839, 13 issues). Edited by John G. Whittier. NOTE: Vol. V ends at Whole No. 156 (Sep 5); Vol. VI No. 1 begins at Whole No. 157 (Sep 12). The Sep 5 (156) front-page masthead MISPRINTS the month as 'Seventh Month 5' (July) -- it is Ninth Month 5 (Sep 5) by sequence between No. 155 (Aug 29) and No. 157 (Sep 12). Flagship structured items: the National Anti-Slavery Convention at Albany (Jul 31 1839, reported 08-15) that the Philadelphia City A-S Society had sent delegates to; and the Anti-Slavery Society of the City and County of Philadelphia's Clarkson Hall meeting (Aug 31 1839) with its Board of Managers roster and Free Produce Convention delegate slate (reported 09-05). articles.headline: Letter from Thomas Morris
articles.author: Thomas Morris
articles.summary: Letter from Thomas Morris (dated Cincinnati, July 22, 1839) explaining that ill health and domestic affairs prevented his attending the National Anti-Slavery Convention at Albany, and setting out his view that the abolition of slavery throughout the civilized world is 'no longer problematical.' Morris, an anti-slavery U.S. Senator from Ohio, reflects on the constitutional questions around slavery and the abolition movement's progress.

articles.headline: The Pennsylvania Freeman -- Volume VI (New Series)
articles.author: John G. Whittier
articles.summary: First number of Volume VI (Whole No. 157, Ninth Month 12, 1839) of the Pennsylvania Freeman under editor John G. Whittier, published by the Eastern District Executive Committee of the Anti-Slavery Society of Pennsylvania. Marks the start of a new volume year for the paper.

events.name: National Anti-Slavery Convention at Albany
events.description: The National Anti-Slavery Convention, held at Albany, N.Y., beginning July 31, 1839 (reported in the Pennsylvania Freeman of Aug 15). Alvan Stewart of New York was chosen President; a slate of Vice-Presidents from across the free states was elected, and Joshua Leavitt, Chauncey L. Knapp, and Henry Grandin appointed Secretaries. The convention debated the 'freeman'/membership question (William Lloyd Garrison's motion to embrace 'all persons' was lost) and welcomed John Scoble of London. The Pennsylvania delegation included Samuel Webb, John G. Whittier, and Thomas Earle. This is the convention the Philadelphia City Anti-Slavery Society had appointed delegates to (see the July 1839 issues).
attendees: moved to admit John Scoble of London

events.name: Anti-Slavery Society of the City and County of Philadelphia -- Clarkson Hall meeting
events.description: Adjourned meeting of the Anti-Slavery Society of the City and County of Philadelphia, held at Clarkson Hall on Eighth Month 31 (Aug 31), 1839, reported in the Pennsylvania Freeman of Sep 5. A Committee of Inquiry (Wm. A. Garrigues, James A. Wright, E. M. Davis, Jacob M. Ellis, James Wood) was appointed to examine the affairs of the first Philadelphia Anti-Slavery Society and the former City and County Society; the meeting also appointed delegates to the Free Produce Convention (see separate entry). Named here are the Committee of Inquiry and the Board of Managers of the former Philadelphia City and County Anti-Slavery Society (James A. Wright, Treasurer).

events.name: Free Produce Convention -- Philadelphia delegates
events.description: Delegates to the Free Produce Convention (to be held Sep 15, 1839), appointed on motion of D. L. Miller Jr. at the Aug 31 meeting of the Anti-Slavery Society of the City and County of Philadelphia (reported in the Pennsylvania Freeman of Sep 5). The slate is a who's-who of Philadelphia free-produce and anti-slavery activists, including many women of the Philadelphia Female Anti-Slavery Society.
